audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'0,63%, Shanghai in calo dello 0,26%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Il S&P 500 è in rialzo del 0,70% a sette mila quattrocento ottantanove punti settantadue, segnale di propensione al rischio. Il VIX è in calo dell'1,81% a quindici virgola settanta, conferma di sentiment risk‑on. Il Dollar Index è in rialzo dello 0,21% a cento virgola zero uno, indica un dollaro più forte. L'oro è in rialzo dell'1,80% a quattro mila centodieciuno dollari l'oncia, riflette la ricerca di valore in un contesto di inflazione moderata. Il Brent è in forte ribasso del 5,80% a ottantaquattro dollari novantotto, spinto da preoccupazioni sulla domanda globale. Il rendimento dei titoli USA a dieci anni è in rialzo dell'1,76% a quattro virgola settantaquattro percento, segnale di aspettative di inflazione più alte. Il BTP a dieci anni è stabile al 3,73%, senza variazione significativa. Il TLT a venti anni è in calo dello 0,66% a ottantadue virgola venticinque, indica pressione sui titoli a lungo termine.

In geopolitica, le tensioni in Ucraina si sono intensificate dopo il rimpasto dei leader militari da parte di Zelenskyy, aumentando il rischio di escalation nella regione. Parallelamente, la chiusura dello Stretto di Hormuz ha limitato il transito di petrolio, contribuendo al ribasso del Brent. Inoltre, le discussioni sulla revisione del NAFTA con la Cina evidenziano una possibile ristrutturazione dei flussi commerciali transatlantici.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. Le recenti analisi di Philip N. Jefferson suggeriscono cautela nelle politiche monetarie, ma non vi sono rilasci ufficiali da considerare nella giornata.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin registra un rialzo dell'uno virgola ottantasei per cento, attestandosi a sessantatremila seicentoquarantasette dollari. Gli ETF futures mostrano un deflusso netto di meno duecentosessantacinque virgola quattro milioni di dollari, segnale di pressione sul mercato. Ethereum avanza di uno virgola ventuno per cento a duemilacentosessantadue dollari, Solana guadagna uno virgola sessantasei per cento a settantatré dollari e cinquanta centesimi, mentre Binance Coin sale di uno virgola zero quattro per cento a cinquecentottantanove dollari e trentaquattro centesimi. L'indice Fear & Greed segna venticinque, classificato come paura estrema, suggerendo cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed down 0.63%, Shanghai down 0.26%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is up 0.7% at 7,489.72 points, signaling risk appetite. The VIX is down 1.81% at 15.7, confirming a risk‑on sentiment. The Dollar Index is up 0.21% at 100.01, indicating a stronger dollar. Gold is up 1.8% at $4,011 per ounce, reflecting a search for value in a moderate‑inflation backdrop. Brent is sharply down 5.8% at $84.98, driven by global demand concerns. The 10‑year U.S. Treasury yield is up 1.76% at 4.74%, a sign of higher inflation expectations. The 10‑year BTP is flat at 3.73%, with no significant change. The 20‑year TLT is down 0.66% at 82.25, indicating pressure on long‑term bonds.

In geopolitics, tensions in Ukraine have intensified after a reshuffle of military leaders by Zelenskyy, raising the risk of escalation in the region. At the same time, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has limited oil transit, contributing to Brent's decline. Additionally, discussions on revising NAFTA with China highlight a possible restructuring of trans‑Atlantic trade flows.

No major macro data scheduled for release today. Recent analyses by Philip N. Jefferson suggest caution on monetary policy, but there are no official releases to consider today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin is up 1.86% at $63,647. Futures ETFs show a net outflow of $265.4 million, signaling pressure on the market. Ethereum advances 1.21% to $2,262, Solana gains 1.66% to $73.5, while Binance Coin rises 1.04% to $549.34. The Fear & Greed index stands at 25, classified as extreme fear, suggesting investor caution.

No macro data on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, visit our platform for the full articles in the Featured Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Is Washington Rewriting the North American Trade Agreement Around China?
articles.snippet: Washington has repeatedly used trade policy and U.S. market access over the past decade to advance broader economic security priorities with its trading partners. The Trump administration’s decision not to renew the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement on July 1, during a mandatory six-year review, is the latest example of this approach. Despite the inclusion in the U.S. trade representative’s announcement that deficits were a prevailing concern, conversations with industry sources and past statements by the administration indicate that ongoing negotiations increasingly focus on limiting Chinese supply chain inputs by embedding economic security principles into the continent’s trade architecture. articles.title: Who pays for tariffs? Insights from recent research
articles.snippet: The Trump administration has mounted many varied claims to support its trade war, but a central argument is that foreigners, not US citizens, pay the price for tariffs. As discussed in our first blog, even if one thought it appropriate to foist tax burdens onto foreigners, there are more efficient and effective ways to do so. Further, multiple practical issues impede the use of so-called optimal tariffs to improve national welfare. Perhaps the biggest of these is that US households and businesses have borne most of the burden of Trump's tariffs in practice. Do foreigners pay for tariffs? The…

articles.title: The Strait of Hormuz closure: What happens to trade and shipping?
articles.snippet: The Strait of Hormuz is a vital passage for world trade, notably for oil and fertilizers. Roughly 88 commercial vessels pass the strait per day, making it one of the world´s most critical maritime chokepoints. The war presents an unprecedented challenge for the maritime industry and shipping traffic. Today, only a handful of vessels can pass while almost 500 vessels are stranded. What are the concrete effects for shipping while the strait is closed and the war is still ongoing? What are the implications for global trade in the absence of commercial vessels passing or transiting? And what will…

articles.title: Georgia’s Kulevi Refinery Replaces Russian Crude With Kazakh, Libyan Oil
articles.snippet: Georgia’s only oil refinery has begun replacing Russian crude with supplies from Kazakhstan and Libya as owner Black Sea Petroleum races to avoid European Union sanctions that will go into effect in January. The Kulevi refinery received and processed Kazakh crude in July and will continue taking Kazakh barrels during August, Black Sea Petroleum said Monday, as reported by Interfax news agency. A Libyan cargo is due to arrive between August 20 and August 30 under a supply agreement signed with an unnamed international company on July 3. The…
